## ASSESSMENT
Fabio presents his own indicator/model ("deep effort"), built out of his personal
reading of Volume Spread Analysis (VSA), formalized as a "law of effort and result":
volume = orders entering, price result = the impact those orders have. He gives two
symmetric single-level definitions (effort-with-no-result = note-worthy reversal
candidate; low-effort-with-outsized-result = a shift in the balance of forces / "path
of least resistance"), then a third construct specific to this video: on a SINGLE
candle where BOTH sides are aggressive, whichever side is absorbed while the other is
rewarded predicts continuation toward the rewarded side even though "the effort is the
same." This last construct is the clearest thing in this video that speaks to the
open question of when absorption implies reversal vs continuation (see U2 below —
ADDRESSES U2, FAB-015).

The rest of the video is a chart walk-through combining the "deep effort" signal with
an external directional-bias tool ("profile framing" / the IVB model, detailed in his
other video cUTsoU-15Tc) and simple trade-management rules: trade only with the day's
bias, require a retest of the model's flagged area before entering, take partial
profit with a runner, and don't fade a structural break without extra confirmation.
No numeric thresholds are given anywhere for what counts as "a lot of volume," "low
effort," "aggressive," or "amazing result" — this is a purely qualitative, chart-read
model. R-multiples quoted in the walk-through (six R, four R, minus one R, etc.) are
EXAMPLE VALUES from specific sessions, not target thresholds.

Clean-slate rule honoured: no Tom Vorwald or other-video material used while
extracting this file.

## RULES EXTRACTED

### FAB-010 — Effort with no result at a level = a level worth noting, potential reversal point
**Source:** Khgj5q1-ln8 @1:03-1:41 | Tier T3 | Tag: DEFINITION
> "I come from a study called volume spread analysis, the VSA. I started this study
> when I was using vertical volume to refine the area of confirmation using the
> relationship between volume and result of price. If I have a wall of orders here
> and I have the price striking here with a lot of volume, I see that there is no
> result, so no follow through of all this effort and the effort is going on. This
> one for me becomes an area, becomes a potential point of reversal, becomes a level
> that I wants to notice."

Definition as stated: a resting "wall of orders" absorbing repeated high-volume
strikes with no price follow-through becomes a flagged level — explicitly only a
"potential" reversal point / a level to watch, not a confirmed reversal signal.
**UNDEFINED:** what counts as "a lot of volume"; what counts as "no result" (minimum
price movement threshold); over what time window the volume accumulates; how many
strikes are needed before flagging the level.

### FAB-011 — Low effort producing an outsized result = the balance of forces has shifted (path of least resistance)
**Source:** Khgj5q1-ln8 @1:41-2:07 | Tier T3 | Tag: DEFINITION
> "At the same time, if I see the market doing an amazing movement with really low
> efforts, okay, on the buy side and I see buyers interacting really aggressively to
> break this level and then I see low effort to make an amazing result. What the
> market is telling me? That the balance between forces here change. And now the
> path of least resistance is on the buy side."

Definition as stated: when a level breaks and the ensuing move is large relative to
the volume that produced it (low effort, high result), this is read as a shift in the
balance of forces, with the "path of least resistance" now favoring that side. This is
the mirror/opposite construct to FAB-010 (high effort, no result).
**UNDEFINED:** what counts as "really low efforts"; what counts as "amazing result";
whether this is measured on the breaking candle alone or over a following sequence.

### FAB-012 — Model design principle: only flag levels with a clear one-sided dominance, for a defined stop
**Source:** Khgj5q1-ln8 @2:20-2:52 | Tier T3 | Tag: PRINCIPLE
> "when you use volume analysis, for example, you can get into consolidation area and
> you can try to execute multiple times taking a lot of break even. So, the logic
> behind was I only want levels where everything is telling me that one side is more
> aggressive than the other. So, having a directional edge and a specific area edge,
> so I can have a clear stop loss in the direction of the model."

Design principle as stated: the model is built to avoid ambiguous consolidation zones
by only flagging levels where the order-flow evidence shows one side clearly more
aggressive than the other, giving both a direction (directional edge) and a location
(area edge) with a clear stop reference.
**UNDEFINED:** how "more aggressive than the other" is measured/thresholded; what
"specific area edge" means geometrically (a price, a zone width).

### FAB-013 — Law of effort and result (foundational principle)
**Source:** Khgj5q1-ln8 @2:59-3:26 | Tier T3 | Tag: PRINCIPLE
> "all this logic behind that you can use here is based on one simple order flow
> concept. And this concept is the law of effort and result. And this is really
> important because you need to understand that volume and price gives you two
> different information. The volume is telling you how many orders are entering.
> The result is telling you how much these orders are having an impact in price
> movement."

Foundational principle as stated: volume (effort) and price movement (result) are two
separate pieces of information; the model's entire logic is built on comparing them.
**UNDEFINED:** no formula/threshold given for combining the two into a signal (that is
what the proprietary "deep effort" tool allegedly does, undisclosed here).

### FAB-014 — Repeated high-volume strikes producing only weak price movement = absorption, do not expect continuation
**Source:** Khgj5q1-ln8 @3:26-3:59 | Tier T3 | Tag: DEFINITION
> "if we are here, for example, on this floor and we see aggressive market
> participants striking on this level with a huge volume. And we see that every time
> the maximum they can do is printing weak. I will not consider a continuation
> because I see that this level getting really interesting from a passive
> participants perspective. They are keeping all these orders, okay, they are
> absorbing here. This is a usual pattern of a absorption."

Definition/rule as stated: when repeated high-volume aggression at a level only ever
produces a weak price result, he explicitly withholds a continuation call ("I will
not consider a continuation") and instead treats it as passive absorption.
**UNDEFINED:** the volume threshold for "huge"; the price-movement ceiling for
"printing weak"; number of repeated strikes required.

### FAB-015 — Same-candle two-sided aggression with asymmetric result, despite similar effort → expect continuation toward the rewarded side
**Source:** Khgj5q1-ln8 @4:11-4:45 | Tier T3 | Tag: SETUP-CONDITION — **ADDRESSES U2**
> "on the other way, when we see aggression of the buyers and at the same candle
> aggression of the sellers, and we see that the sellers are completely absorbed and
> the buyers are rewarded, what the market is telling us here is that in this battle
> they have maybe the same effort, but the result it's heavy skew on the upside. So,
> what I can do as an analyst, I can understand that the probability that we continue
> higher, so we go to tap into this high is the biggest one, but the effort is the
> same. Maybe you have the same effort from aggressive buyers and aggressive sellers,
> but the sellers are completely absorbed."

Discriminator as stated: this is a different construct from FAB-010/FAB-014 (one-sided
persistent absorption with no counter-aggression, flagged only as a level to watch).
Here BOTH sides are aggressive on the SAME candle, effort is roughly comparable, but
the result is asymmetric — one side's aggression is completely absorbed while the
other side is rewarded (price moves in its favor). He states this raises the
probability of continuation toward the rewarded side, explicitly despite "the effort
is the same." This is the closest thing in this video to a stated rule for when
absorption of one side implies CONTINUATION (in the surviving/rewarded side's
direction) rather than a reversal signal.
**UNDEFINED:** how "same effort" is measured/tolerance for "maybe"; how much
asymmetry in result counts as "heavy skew"; single-candle only, per his wording — no
statement of what happens if the asymmetry unfolds over multiple candles.

### FAB-016 — Model triggers: a pre-framed area + a "deep effort" directional-skew reading is the entry signal on approach/retest
**Source:** Khgj5q1-ln8 @5:13-5:52 | Tier T3 | Tag: PROCEDURE
> "the logic of putting in relationship price, volume and putting also in
> relationship the granularity of the order inside. And on this we have a proprietary
> model that is capable of filtering all the noise and is giving you what I like to
> call triggers, triggers to potentially execute. And it's giving you an edge when you
> have, for example, frame your area, your point of interest maybe using price
> action, using everything, and you approach the level back again here and you have
> your deep effort telling you, 'Look that from this moment we are askew on the
> downside.' So, you have your area. And what this is telling you that the
> probability from this box on is to continue lower."

Procedure as stated: (1) frame a point of interest by any external method (price
action, "everything"), (2) wait for price to return/approach that level, (3) at that
moment read the "deep effort" tool's directional skew — a trigger to potentially
execute in the direction the tool shows.
**UNDEFINED:** the internal mechanics of "deep effort" (a proprietary/undisclosed
tool — what volumes, timeframe, or filter it uses); what "askew" numerically means;
how far price must approach the level to count as a valid retest.

### FAB-017 — Partial profit-taking and stop adjustment when an opposing "deep effort" signal appears
**Source:** Khgj5q1-ln8 @5:52-6:36 | Tier T3 | Tag: RISK
> "when you see a an opposite area on the buy side, you can understand that now this
> selling pressure it's almost exhausted and the probability instead of continuing
> that you will go up to this level it's higher. So, the consideration that you can
> make is that it's not worth to risk all this profit that I make just to make an
> additional small movement by risking all this profit. So, I take it out my
> position. What I do? I consider putting stop below. So, if the market wants to
> continue, I'm into the position again. I took profit on the first one and I have my
> liquidation here. This is a smart way of managing trades."

Rule as stated: while in a position, if the model flags an opposing-direction area
(read as near-exhaustion of the current move), take profit rather than risk it for a
small additional move, and place a new stop below the exit so a resumption of the
original direction re-enters the trade.
**UNDEFINED:** how much of the position to close (he does not give a fraction here);
exact stop distance below the exit level.

**Source:** Khgj5q1-ln8 @7:01-7:22, reinforced @9:05-9:13, @11:22-11:28 | Tier T3 | Tag: SETUP-CONDITION

**UNDEFINED:** exactly how the day's bias is computed (external to this video); what

Rule as stated: use two targets — a partial exit (example given: 50% of full/planned

### FAB-020 — A momentum-flagged area that price never retests cannot be taken (retest required for entry)
**Source:** Khgj5q1-ln8 @7:55-8:14 | Tier T3 | Tag: SETUP-CONDITION
> "The second area that gave us is this one. This one it's a momentum setup. Why
> momentum setup? Because it closed above it and never test. So, this one you
> couldn't take because the market don't give you a test. Here it gives you an area,
> immediately test, gives you another area, immediately test, so you could make a lot

Rule as stated: a "momentum setup" area is one the market closes above without
retesting it; such an area is explicitly untradeable under this model ("you couldn't
take because the market don't give you a test") — an entry requires an actual retest
of the flagged area.
**UNDEFINED:** what counts as an acceptable retest (proximity/time tolerance).

### FAB-021 — Do not take a counter-trend trade on a structural break; wait for a separate directional confirmation
**Source:** Khgj5q1-ln8 @10:01-10:24 | Tier T3 | Tag: RISK / SETUP-CONDITION
> "the market break the structure. This is the beginning of the range. So, when it
> breaks on the opposite side using the deep effort, I don't go trend counter trend on
> this one. So, I need to wait that we have another confirmation of directional."

Rule as stated: when price structurally breaks to the opposite side of the standing
range/bias and the "deep effort" tool flags that break, he does not trade counter to
his prior trend read on that break alone — he requires an additional, separate
directional confirmation before acting.
**UNDEFINED:** what qualifies as "another confirmation of directional" (no specific
signal named); how long to wait for it.

Rule as stated: in a long-momentum context, entries are taken on retests of
model-flagged areas, with the protective stop placed below the retested area
("covering below the areas") to capture favorable risk-to-reward.
**UNDEFINED:** exact stop distance below the area (not quantified).
